elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: The inserted warranty says only that "for thirty (30) days following performance, the services will be performed in conformity with this Agreement"; there is no professional/workmanlike or industry-standards standard anywhere in Section 9 or elsewhere.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: "the Site and any software delivered hereunder will conform in all material respects to its documentation".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: The inserted period is "for ninety (90) days following delivery", not twelve months.
Services are warranted only "for thirty (30) days following performance".

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "HDI shall, at the Company's election, repair or replace the non-conforming software or services...".
"...or refund the amounts paid for them."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the inserted paragraph or in retained Section 9(a)-(b), which cover only corporate existence, authority, enforceability, non-conflict and the Globix acknowledgment.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious code / virus warranty is present in the inserted language or elsewhere in Section 9.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: "HDI warrants that (1) for ninety (90) days following delivery, the Site and any software delivered hereunder will conform in all material respects to its documentation" — exactly 90 days, satisfying "at least 90 days". The deterministic check "warranty period >= 90 days or expressed in months/years" reported ok:false, but on inspection the operative text does state ninety (90) days, so the regex result is a mechanical miss rather than a substantive shortfall.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: "(2) for thirty (30) days following performance, the services will be performed in conformity with this Agreement" — a 30-day services warranty period with a stated performance standard (conformity with the Agreement).

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "For any breach of this warranty, HDI shall, at the Company's election, repair or replace the non-conforming software or services...".
"...or refund the amounts paid for them." Remedy applies to "any breach of this warranty", so it covers both the software and services limbs.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: 90-day software/Site conformance-to-documentation warranty, 30-day services warranty, and a single remedy sentence covering repair, replacement and refund for "any breach of this warranty". The failing deterministic period check is a mechanical artifact — the operative text reads "ninety (90) days following delivery".

Preferred level fails on four elements the drafter would have to add: a professional and workmanlike/industry-standards services standard, a 12-month software period (currently 90 days), a 90-day services period (currently 30 days), a compliance-with-applicable-laws warranty, and a no-malicious-code warranty.

Minimality holds: the insertion adds only the conformance warranty, the two periods and the three remedies, with no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no added damages categories, no notice/claim procedure and no disclaimer carve-out (none is needed because the document contains no "AS IS" or implied-warranty disclaimer to carve out of). Note that "at the Company's election" is more aggressive than the playbook model language ("at Vendor's option"), but it is a variation within the remedy elements rather than an extra requirement, and it benefits us.

Intent is preserved: retained Sections 9(a) and 9(b) (mutual corporate warranties and the Globix acknowledgment) are untouched and are not contradicted; the warranty runs in the correct direction (HDI, the developer/host, warrants to the Company, our client); no term is left undefined and no cross-reference dangles.

Drafting nit for the drafter to clean up (not a completeness or intent failure): the rationale and comment describe the insertion as "new Section 9(c)", but the rendered paragraph carries no "(c)" designation. Add the subsection letter so the new warranty can be cross-referenced consistently with 9(a) and 9(b).

Optional polish, not required by the fallback checklist: "refund the amounts paid for them" could be tightened to "the fees paid for the non-conforming software or Services" to avoid argument over which amounts are refundable.
